# share/

## Purpose
Read-only share links for a report pack: mint, list, revoke (authenticated) and resolve a token (unauthenticated). Tables `share_links` and `share_link_views`, migration 610.

## Caller contract
- Authenticated: `pages/api/accounting/share/links*` under `withAuth`, company from the session.
- Unauthenticated: `pages/share/[token].tsx` (getServerSideProps only). **The resolver runs on the pool connection, which is a SUPERUSER and bypasses RLS** — the `share_links` / `share_link_views` policies are `TO app_user` and no unauthenticated visitor has a session to carry a tenant GUC. The `company_id` predicate carried by every downstream query IS the tenancy control here; RLS is the second line, not the first. Do not "fix" this by making the public page run as `app_user`.
- `shareParams.ts` and `shareTtl.ts` are db-free and re-export nothing. `clampTtlDays` comes from `shareTtl`; `SharePackParams` and `canonicalParamsHash` come from `@/modules/accounting/services/reports/packParamsHash`, which pulls in `node:crypto` and is therefore server-only (`import type` is safe; a value import from a browser component fails the webpack build, guarded by `tests/unit/components-bundle-safety/shareBundleSafety.test.ts`).

## Main signatures
- `createShareLink({ companyId, userId, params, label?, ttlDays? })` → `{ link, token }`. The raw token is returned ONCE and never again. Throws `ShareLinkLimitError` at `MAX_LIVE_LINKS` (100).
- `listShareLinks(companyId)` / `revokeShareLink(companyId, id, userId) → boolean`.
- `resolveShareLink(token, ctx) → { status: 'ok' | 'expired' | 'revoked' | 'not_found' | 'rate_limited' }`; `commitShareView(link, ctx) → 'served' | 'withdrawn'`; `recordShareView(link, outcome, ctx, exec?)`; `recordUnmatchedView(ctx, exec?)` for a token that matched no row.
- `buildSharedPack(link) → SharedPack`; `stripOmittedSections(pack)`; `parseSharePackParams(raw)`, `mintShareToken`/`hashShareToken`/`isShareTokenShape`. `canonicalParamsHash` lives in `reports/packParamsHash.ts`.

## Business rules
- **Neutral 404.** Unknown, expired, revoked and *failed* are ONE outcome to the caller: same page, same status, same props. Distinguishing them makes the route an oracle — a prober could tell "never existed" from "withdrawn", which is a fact about the company. Rate limiting is the only separate answer. The whole of `getServerSideProps` runs inside one `try`, so a throw from the resolver, the limiter or the audit write degrades to that page rather than to Next's 500.
- **Equal work, not just equal answers.** All three dead outcomes write one `share_link_views` row, so they cannot be told apart by timing. An unmatched token writes a row naming NO link and NO company (`outcome = 'not_found'`, migration 613); a null `company_id` is in no tenant's RLS set, so the row belongs to the platform. A token of the wrong SHAPE is the one exception: it is rejected before the limiter and audits nothing, because it was never a token and auditing it would be an unbounded unauthenticated INSERT.
- Expiry and revocation are checked on every view, on the row the lookup found. Withdrawal is immediate; there is no TTL to wait out and no expiry embedded in the token.
- Only the sha256 of a token is stored. Never log a raw token, a token hash or a URL from this path — put `redactShareToken` (`@/lib/observability/redactShareToken` — there is no `@/lib/observability` barrel) around any URL that is logged.
- The rate limiter fails CLOSED: an outage answers `rate_limited`, never `ok`.
- Every hit past the limiter is audited, dead links and unmatched tokens included. A live view is audited by `commitShareView` AFTER the pack is built, never before.
- **Liveness is checked TWICE, and the second check is the race-free one.** `resolveShareLink` reads `revoked_at` once; the pack build between the two reads the whole ledger twice, and a sender revoking during it is exactly when they most mean it. `commitShareView` therefore carries `revoked_at IS NULL AND expires_at > NOW()` in its own UPDATE and `RETURNING id`: under READ COMMITTED the predicate is re-evaluated after the row lock, so a revoke that committed mid-build is seen. Zero rows means the link died mid-build — the audit records `revoked` or `expired` (read back in the same transaction, so the trail does not claim a withdrawal for a timeout), no `ok` row is written, and the function answers `withdrawn` so the page serves the neutral 404 instead of the pack it has already built.
- Only approved commentary is published (`status = 'approved'`). Annotations are never on this path.
- `OMITTED_SECTIONS` sections are stripped SERVER-SIDE, so "Not included on shared links." is true of the document, not just of the rendering.
- Creation is serialised by a per-company `pg_advisory_xact_lock`; the count guard alone lets two concurrent creates pass at 99.
- **Reading the link LIST is owner/admin/manager** (`canReadSharingSurface`, `services/reports/sharingAccess.ts`). `withWriteAccess` gates mutating methods only — its `allowedRoles` option says nothing about a GET — so the route checks the role itself. The list is who a pack was shared with, when the link expires, who minted it and how often an outsider opened it.

## Recent changes
- 2026-09-06: `commitShareView` re-checks revocation and expiry in its own UPDATE, so a revoke landing while the pack was being built stops the response instead of being recorded as a plain `ok`.
- 2026-09-06: migration 613. An unmatched token is audited too, with a null link and company, so the three dead outcomes cost the same; and the resolve moved inside the page's `try` so a throw is the neutral 404 rather than a 500.
- 2026-09-06: `cash_flow` joined `OMITTED_SECTIONS`. `buildSectionData` synthesizes it (operating cash flow = net profit, investing and financing = 0), which is a placeholder on the owner's screen and a false statement of cash movement on a document sent to a bank. It returns when the section is built from the ledger.
- 2026-09-06: the public page reads the client IP through `getClientIp` (`@/lib/rateLimit`) — LAST forwarded hop, pentest H8 — instead of its own first-hop parser. `user_agent` is bounded once, in `recordShareView`.
- 2026-09-06: `/share/` is excluded from the service worker in both `public/sw.js` and `_app.tsx`; a cached pack served offline after revocation defeats the only control the sender has.

## Known follow-ups
- The app-wide `AuthProvider` in `_app.tsx` runs on `/share/<token>` too, so the public page fires `/api/auth/me` and takes a 401 the recipient never sees a consequence of. Nothing leaks — the 401 is the correct answer for a caller with no session, and the page renders entirely from `getServerSideProps` — but a third party being shown one document should not be causing an auth call at all. WS2 is adding a `skipFetch` gate to that provider; extending it to `/share/*` (via `isSharePath`) is the fix, at integration, once both branches are on master.
